record.reference: Shepherd of Hermas — Vision 3, section iv

source.text: Ἀποκριθεὶς λέγω αὐτῇ· Κυρία, μεγάλως καὶ θαυμαστῶς ἔχει τὸ πρᾶγμα τοῦτο. οἱ δὲ νεανίσκοι οἱ ἓξ οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες τίνες εἰσίν, κυρία; Οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἅγιοι ἄγγελοι τοῦ Θεοῦ οἱ πρῶτοι κτισθέντες, οἷς παρέδωκεν ὁ Κύριος πᾶσαν τὴν κτίσιν αὐτοῦ, αὔξειν καὶ οἰκοδομεῖν καὶ δεσπόζειν τῆς κτίσεως πάσης. διὰ τούτων οὖν τελεσθήσεται ἡ οἰκοδομὴ τοῦ πύργου. 2. Οἱ δὲ ἕτεροι οἱ παραφέροντες τοὺς λίθους τίνες εἰσίν; Καὶ αὐτοὶ ἅγιοι ἄγγελοι τοῦ Θεοῦ· οὗτοι δὲ οἱ ἓξ ὑπερέχοντες αὐτούς εἰσιν. συντελεσθήσεται οὖν ἡ οἰκοδομὴ τοῦ πύργου, καὶ πάντες ὁμοῦ εὐφρανθήσονται κύκλῳ τοῦ πύργου καὶ δοξάσουσιν τὸν Θεόν, ὅτι ἐτελέσθη ἡ οἰκοδομὴ τοῦ πύργου. 3. ἐπηρώτησα αὐτὴν λέγων· Κυρία, ἤθελον γνῶναι τῶν λίθων τὴν ἔξοδον καὶ τὴν δύναμιν αὐτῶν, ποταπή ἐστιν. ἀποκριθεῖσά μοι λέγει· Οὐχ ὅτι σὺ ἐκ πάντων ἀξιώτερος εἶ ἵνα σοι ἀποκαλυφθῇ· ἄλλοι γάρ σου πρότεροι εἰσιν καὶ βελτίονές σου, οἷς ἔδει ἀποκαλυφθῆναι τὰ ὁράματα ταῦτα· ἀλλ’ ἵνα δοξασθῇ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Θεοῦ, σοὶ ἀπεκαλύφθη καὶ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται διὰ τοὺς διψύχους, τοὺς διαλογιζομένους ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν εἰ ἄρα ἔστιν ταῦτα ἢ οὐκ ἔστιν. λέγε αὐτοῖς ὅτι ταῦτα πάντα ἐστὶν ἀληθῆ, καὶ οὐθὲν ἔξωθέν ἐστιν τῆς ἀληθείας, ἀλλὰ πάντα ἰσχυρὰ καὶ βέβαια καὶ τεθεμελιωμένα ἐστίν.
source.label: Vision 3, section iv

translation.text:
Answering[1], I say to her, "Lady, this matter is great and marvelous. And the six young men who are building—who are they, Lady?"

"These are the holy angels of God, the first-created,[1] to whom the Lord entrusted all his creation—to make it grow and to build it up and to rule over all creation. By these, therefore, the building of the tower[5] will be brought to completion.[4]"

2[2]. "And the others who are carrying the stones—who are they?"

"They too are holy angels of God; but these six are superior to them. The building of the tower, then, will be brought to completion, and all together will rejoice around the tower and will glorify God, because the building of the tower has been completed."

3. I asked her, saying, "Lady, I wished to know the outcome[2] of the stones and their power—what sort it is."

Answering me, she says, "It is not because you are more worthy than all that it is revealed to you; for there are others before you and better than you, to whom it was fitting that these visions should be revealed. But in order that the name of God might be glorified, it has been revealed to you and will be revealed, for the sake of the double-minded[3]—those who reason within their hearts whether these things are so or not. Tell them that all these things are true, and nothing is outside the truth; rather[5][4][3], all are strong and sure and well-founded."

footnotes.text: 'First-created' translates οἱ πρῶτοι κτισθέντες. Alternatives include 'first in rank' or 'first appointed', but the Greek participle naturally means 'created'.
The word rendered 'origin' is ἔξοδος, which can mean 'coming forth' or 'issue'; in context it refers to the stones' emergence and provenance.
'Double-minded' (διψύχος) appears in early Christian moral vocabulary; compare James 1:8; 4:8 for similar usage.
Two related verbs are used for 'be brought to completion' in this section (τελεσθήσεται and συντελεσθήσεται), both conveying consummation of the work.
Within Hermas, the tower is the central symbol for the people of God being built; see Vision 3 overall for the imagery's development.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Respectful form of address to the female figure; "Lady" preserves dignity without implying ownership.
Common Koine sense for male youths; avoids archaic tone while keeping age nuance.
Plain participial rendering keeps the building metaphor active.
Standard early Christian sense of ἄγγελος; "holy" kept as an attributive adjective.
Participial phrase naturally denotes sequence in creation; retained literally to reflect Hermas' angelology.
In stewardship contexts παραδίδωμι conveys "entrust" (assign responsibility), fitting the angelic charge over creation.
Default rendering for κτίσις; broad cosmic scope is explicit in "all creation".
Dynamic infinitive paraphrase keeps transitivity clear; the object is creation's growth.
"Build up" maintains the constructive nuance and ties to the tower imagery.
Idiomatic English for exercising lordship; avoids the slavery connotations of "master" in modern English.
Passive form foregrounds the work's completion by agency (the angels) without overstating their independence.
Syn-prefixed cognate emphasizes culmination; same English rendering preserves sense, with note provided.
Parapherō here denotes transport; "carrying" is natural English.
Conveys comparative rank/status in clear English.
Standard rendering for the deponent future passive of εὐφραίνω in Koine contexts.
Concise spatial preposition; context already implies circular gathering.
Aorist indicative with resultant sense in visionary report; perfect-like translation fits English idiom.
Within Hermas' context of stones "coming out" for the tower, ἔξοδος denotes their emergence/origin; "origin" is concise.
Default rendering; keeps the abstract noun's force.
Comparative of ἄξιος; "worthy" fits Hermas' moral register.
Temporal priority is emphasized; not necessarily rank.
Plain comparative of ἀγαθός via βελτίων; "better" suits tone.
Hermas often uses ἔδει with the sense of propriety/fitness; "fitting" is slightly softer than "necessary."
Maintains the visual aspect of the experiences described.
Standard theologically-loaded rendering of δοξάζω.
Conventional early Christian term; preserves moral diagnosis of inner division.
Keeps the sense of inward deliberation without importing adversarial tone.
Biblical/early Christian anthropological term; standard rendering.
Plain adjective; no need for variation.
Metaphorical spatial preposition; "outside the truth" preserves Hermas' absolute claim.
Default theological term.
Pairs well with βέβαια in English rhythm while retaining meaning.
Conveys stability/reliability alongside ἰσχυρά.
Echoes building imagery; idiomatic English for a secure foundation.

theological_decisions.issue: Status of the six builders as 'the first-created' angels (οἱ πρῶτοι κτισθέντες)
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render literally as 'the first-created', indicating primacy in creation among the angels.
theological_decisions.rationale: The participle κτισθέντες most naturally denotes having been created; Hermas elsewhere ranks angelic beings. The literal reading preserves his angelology without importing later systematic constraints.

theological_decisions.issue: Scope of angelic stewardship over creation (πᾶσαν τὴν κτίσιν… δεσπόζειν τῆς κτίσεως πάσης)
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Cosmic scope: the angels are entrusted with all creation to foster growth, build, and rule it.
theological_decisions.rationale: The repetition of κτίσις with πᾶσα ('all') and the triad of infinitives suggests a broad stewardship, not merely ecclesial administration.
Per project policy, κύριος as a divine title is rendered 'Lord'; 'Master' could confuse with δεσπόζειν and modern connotations.
'Double-minded' is a recognized early Christian moral term capturing inner division; it also resonates with Hermas' paraenetic emphasis without importing NT phrasing wholesale.

theological_decisions.issue: 'Nothing is outside the truth' (οὐθὲν ἔξωθέν ἐστιν τῆς ἀληθείας)
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Maintain the absolute-sounding claim as stated.
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas asserts the reliability of the visions against doubters. The spatial metaphor 'outside' intensifies the claim and fits his imagery-laden style.

review_passes.summary: The draft is highly accurate and captures Hermas's tone well. A few minor adjustments were made to preserve the historical present tense (λέγω, λέγει) and participial structures, and to remove an added "She said" that is absent in the Greek. Additionally, "what sort they are" was corrected to "what sort it is" to reflect the singular Greek verb (ποταπή ἐστιν) referring to the power/origin.
issues_found: "I answered and said" flattens the present tense of λέγω and the participial structure of Ἀποκριθεὶς.
"She said," is added in verse 1 without a corresponding verb in the Greek text.
"what sort they are" translates the singular ποταπή ἐστιν, which agrees with the feminine singular δύναμιν/ἔξοδον; "what sort it is" is more accurate.
"She answered me and said" flattens the present tense of λέγει and the participial structure of ἀποκριθεῖσά.

translation.text: Answering me, she says, "It is not because you are more worthy than all that it is revealed to you; for there are others before you and better than you, to whom it was fitting that these visions should be revealed. But in order that the name of God might be glorified, it has been revealed to you and will be revealed, for the sake of the double-minded—those who reason within their hearts whether these things are so or not. Tell them that all these things are true, and nothing is outside the truth; rather, all are strong and sure and well-founded."

base_translation.text: Answering me, she says, "It is not because you are more worthy than all that it is revealed to you; for there are others before you and better than you, to whom it was fitting that these visions should be revealed. But in order that the name of God might be glorified, it has been revealed to you and will be revealed, for the sake of the double-minded—those who reason within their hearts whether these things are so or not. Tell them that all these things are true, and nothing is outside the truth; rather, all are strong and sure and well-founded."

translation.text: She answered me, “These visions are not being shown to you because you are more worthy than everyone else. Others came before you who are better than you, and it would have been fitting for these visions to be shown to them. But they have been shown to you and will continue to be shown so that God’s name may be glorified. They are also for those who cannot make up their minds and wonder in their hearts whether these things are true. Tell them that all these things are true. Nothing in them departs from the truth. They are firm, certain, and built on a solid foundation.”
